title: Introducing Durable Agents
summary: Blink can now build AI agents in your apps that continuously execute long-horizon tasks, like research and batch jobs that keep going after you close the tab.
body_markdown:
On this page 8 sections


1. 01 Most AI apps stop the moment you look away
2. 02 A durable agent finishes the job on its own
3. 03 Blink decides when your app needs one
4. 04 Build a durable AI agent without writing code
5. 05 Every source is a page the agent actually read
6. 06 What this means if you run a business
7. 07 The honest limits
8. 08 Start with one list


Blink can now build AI agents in your Blink apps that continuously execute long-horizon tasks.


We call them Durable Agents.


Describe an app that researches a market, writes a brief for every company on a list, or turns one product photo into a full photo shoot. Blink builds the job as an agent that runs on your app's own server, saves every step, and keeps going until the job is done. That includes after you close the tab.


You don't have to ask for it. Blink works out that the job needs one.


## Most AI apps stop the moment you look away


Most AI apps are built like a chat window. You ask, the page calls the AI, the answer comes back.


That works for one question. It breaks the moment the job gets real.


A sales brief for 30 companies is 30 site visits, 30 news searches and 30 rounds of writing. That takes several minutes.


In a typical AI-built app, all of that runs inside your browser tab. Close the laptop lid and it stops. Refresh by accident and the half-finished briefs are gone. One slow website and the whole batch fails.


So the app demos well, then falls over on Monday morning with a real list.


The old way: an AI job dies with the browser tab. The new way: a durable agent keeps working on the server.


Blink


## A durable agent finishes the job on its own


A durable agent moves the job off the page and onto your app's own server.


The page starts the run and gets out of the way. The agent works through the job in steps — search, read, write — and saves each step as it finishes.


That one change fixes every failure above:


- **Close the tab.** The run keeps going. Open the app later, on any device, and the finished work is there.
- **A step fails.** Only that step retries. Nothing already done is redone or paid for twice.
- **The server restarts.** The run picks up at the first unfinished step.
- **Watch it work.** Every open page shows live progress, like "Researching company 2 of 5", with results appearing one by one.
- **Keep the results.** Finished reports are saved to your app's database and listed in each user's history.


In the demo above, we closed the tab one company into a batch of five. A minute later we opened the app again. The first brief was done and the agent was already on the second.


A sales-brief app on company 2 of 5, with the first brief already finished


Blink


## Blink decides when your app needs one


Nobody asks for "durable execution". Business users ask for outcomes: a lead researcher, a market analyst, a report generator.


So Blink reads what the app has to do, not the words you used. When the core feature is a long-horizon task, Blink builds a durable agent automatically.


We tested this on real prompts from Blink users. Blink now spots 92% of the apps that need a durable agent, up from 12% before.


It recognizes four kinds of job:


- **Research** — several web searches turned into a report with sources
- **Batch work** — AI run on every item in a list: companies, leads, URLs, files
- **Staged generation** — each step builds on the last, like an outline, then sections
- **Autonomous agents** — working through a goal with tools, over many steps


A chatbot that answers one message at a time stays a chatbot. A single AI call stays a single call. You only get the heavier setup when the job needs it.


## Build a durable AI agent without writing code


Paste one of these as your first message on Blink:


```text
Build an app where I paste a list of up to 30 company websites and it writes
a one-page sales brief for each company: what they do, who they sell to,
recent news, and a suggested opening line for a cold email.


```


```text
Build an AI analyst that writes a complete, well-researched market analysis
on any industry I type in: market size, key players, trends, risks and
opportunities, with sources. Keep a library of the analyses.


```


```text
Build a lead researcher: I upload a CSV of leads (name, company, website) and
for each lead it researches the company online and writes a personalized first
email. I want to see results come in and export them.


```


Blink builds the page, the backend and the agent, deploys it, and tests the whole flow before handing the app back. Sign-in, the database and hosting come included, so there is nothing else to set up.


The first prompt above built the app in the demo in 12 minutes. Here is one of the five briefs it wrote:


A finished sales brief with recent news and a suggested cold-email opening line


Blink


## Every source is a page the agent actually read


A research app is only as good as its citations. An AI asked to "cite sources" without real results in hand will invent them.


Blink's research agents search the live web and build the Sources list from the pages they actually read. Every link goes somewhere real. Web search now works with any AI model your app uses.


## What this means if you run a business


You can hand real work to an app you built in an afternoon, then walk away:


- **Sales teams** paste Monday's prospect list and come back to a brief and an opener for each account.
- **Agencies** run a site and reputation audit for a prospect while they're on the discovery call.
- **Analysts** queue a market scan at 5pm and read it with their coffee.
- **Operators** let a batch of product photos, listings or summaries finish overnight.


Before, this needed an engineer to set up job queues, retries and a worker server. Now it takes one sentence.


## The honest limits


- **Pro plans and above.** Durable agents run in Blink Backend. On Free and Starter, Blink builds the job to run in the page, and it stops if the tab closes.
- **A redeploy pauses runs for up to about 5 minutes.** When you publish a backend change mid-run, the run waits for the interrupted step to time out, then resumes. No work is repeated.
- **Big jobs spend more credits.** Thirty companies means thirty times the AI calls of one. Your app's AI usage is in Settings → Usage.


## Start with one list


Open Blink, paste the sales-brief prompt above, and give it five company websites. Close the tab while it runs. Come back to five finished briefs.
